Mali — 19th-highest-population country. `ml-cpi-social-protection.json` already covers CPI/EHCVM/AFRISTAT's Bamako headquarters; this round goes to the commune fiscal tier. Standout finding, a new pattern for this branch: Mali's CURRENT collectivités code (Loi n°2023-004, 2023, adopted under the transition government) is textually LESS specific on fiscal transfers than the code it replaced — the abrogated 2017 code named FNACT and a hard 30% minimum transfer floor; the 2023 code drops both, leaving transfer amounts to unquantified 'dotations et subventions spéciales.' A regression in statutory specificity, the mirror image of the 'enabling law without operative practice' pattern already documented for Angola/Mozambique.

reports.title: Loi n°2023-004 du 13 mars 2023 portant Code des Collectivités Territoriales (code en vigueur)
reports.publisher: Conseil National de Transition / Présidence de la Transition du Mali
reports.description: Mali's current, governing collectivités code, verified via the Journal Officiel text (mirrored on ILO's NATLEX). Art. 22(9): communal councils deliberate on "la fixation des taux des impôts et taxes communaux dans le cadre des bases et des maxima fixés par la loi." Art. 155 states the fiscal-legality principle: "Le principe de la légalité de l'impôt implique que la création des impôts et taxes est du domaine de la loi. L'organe délibérant de la Collectivité territoriale, par sa délibération, fixe le taux des impôts et taxes locaux dans la limite du plafond déterminé par la loi." Art. 182 defines collectivité resources: "1. des ressources fiscales qui comprennent: les impôts d'Etat transférés aux Collectivités territoriales; les impôts et taxes locaux directs; les impôts et taxes locaux indirects. 2. des produits par nature...3. des ressources budgétaires qui sont constituées des dotations et subventions spéciales de l'Etat aux Collectivités territoriales." Art. 241 ("De la solidarité et de la coopération entre collectivités territoriales") only cross-references generically: "conformément aux textes en vigueur," without naming a specific fund. Art. 251 explicitly abrogates the predecessor code: "La présente loi abroge la Loi n°2017-051 du..." KEY FINDING: ANICT and FNACT are NOT NAMED by acronym anywhere in this current code (confirmed via full-text grep), and no explicit transfer percentage appears anywhere — unlike the 2017 code it replaced, this code leaves the state→collectivité transfer rate entirely unquantified in statute, delegated to undefined "dotations et subventions spéciales."
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument, currently in force.

reports.title: Loi n°2017-051 du 02 octobre 2017 portant Code des Collectivités Territoriales (ABROGÉE par la Loi n°2023-004)
reports.publisher: Présidence de la République du Mali
reports.description: The predecessor collectivités code, verified via a FAOLEX mirror of the Journal Officiel text (06 October 2017), promulgated by then-President Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta. Art. 28 creates FNACT: "L'Etat garantit et organise le principe de solidarité entre les Collectivités territoriales. Il est créé à cet effet un Fonds national d'Appui aux Collectivités territoriales (FNACT)." Art. 29 sets an explicit numeric transfer floor and a natural-resource retrocession clause: "L'Etat procède annuellement à un transfert des ressources budgétaires aux Collectivités territoriales. Le taux de transfert qui ne peut être inférieur à 30% en 2018...sont définies par la loi de finances. L'Etat rétrocède aux Collectivités territoriales concernées un pourcentage des revenus issus de l'exploitation, sur leur territoire, des ressources naturelles." This is the clearest verbatim primary-source statement found in this branch's Mali research establishing both FNACT's legal creation and a hard minimum transfer rate. It is no longer in force, expressly abrogated by Art. 251 of ml-loi-2023-004-code-collectivites — kept in the corpus as a historical/superseded citation documenting the specificity the current code dropped.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument, no longer in force (superseded 2023).

reports.title: ANICT (Agence Nationale d'Investissement des Collectivités Territoriales) — présentation institutionnelle et statistiques cumulées
reports.description: ANICT's own official site, verified directly. Homepage aggregate statistic (own voice, cumulative/undated): "+ de 25 000 Projets réalisés" / "+ de 340 Milliards de FCFA Mobilisés par les collectivités auprès de l'ANICT." ANICT's own presentation page references FNACT as an active reporting line ("Rapports d'exécution technique et financière du FNACT" appears as a menu item), and its 'outils de financement' page describes FNACT as comprising "5 guichets" (windows) addressing investment-resource access, training, operational support, plus DIN-DER (regional council support) and CPER (Région/District support) — but no distribution-key percentage or per-collectivité transfer formula was located on ANICT's own site despite checking its financing-tools and documentation/policy pages directly.
reports.cadence_note: Cumulative/undated institutional statistic on ANICT's own site, not tied to a specific report edition.

reports.title: Loi n°2024-017 du 11 décembre 2024 portant ratification du Traité portant création de la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES)
reports.publisher: Conseil National de Transition / Présidence de la Transition du Mali (Journal Officiel)
reports.description: The Journal Officiel's own text of Mali's ratification of the AES Confederation Treaty, verified directly (Journal Officiel 2024-29). Verbatim: "LOI N°2024-017 DU 11 DECEMBRE 2024 PORTANT RATIFICATION DE L'ORDONNANCE N°2024-015/PT-RM DU 20 SEPTEMBRE 2024 AUTORISANT LA RATIFICATION DU TRAITE PORTANT CREATION DE LA CONFEDERATION DES ETATS DU SAHEL (AES), ADOPTE A NIAMEY (NIGER), LE 06 JUILLET 2024, LORS DU PREMIER SOMMET DES CHEFS D'ETAT DE L'AES," promulgated by "Général d'Armée Assimi GOITA," Bamako, 11 December 2024. This law ratifies the Confederation Treaty only — it does NOT itself discuss the ECOWAS/CEDEAO exit (confirmed via full-text grep: zero matches for "CEDEAO"). A companion Conseil des Ministres communiqué (CM N°2024-36/SGG, 28 August 2024) discusses adoption of the ratification measures in similar terms, also without naming CEDEAO; that communiqué is only located on a third-party mirror (its exact CM-numbering format and content are cross-validated against maliweb.net and primature.ml's own current template, but it could not be found still live on primature.ml itself).
reports.cadence_note: One-off ratification instrument, not a periodic report.

dependencies.basis: Article 251 of the current code explicitly repeals its predecessor by number: "La présente loi abroge la Loi n°2017-051 du..." — a direct textual cross-reference confirmed in both documents.

Both documents independently describe the same event: the AES Confederation Treaty adopted at the first AES Heads-of-State summit in Niamey on 6 July 2024. Mali's ratification law and Niger's Ministry of Finance article each confirm this date, location, and treaty in their own voice — recorded as 'cites' since the two documents independently corroborate the same underlying event rather than one being derived from the other.

_dropped.edge: Mali government document -> substantive discussion of the ECOWAS/CEDEAO withdrawal decision itself (not just the AES Confederation Treaty)
_dropped.why: The single most promising lead (koulouba.ml, a page titled 'Conseil extraordinaire des ministres: les raisons et opportunités du retrait du Mali de la CEDEAO') failed to load on two independent attempts (ROBOTS_DISALLOWED / ConnectTimeout) this session — a genuine access failure, not a confirmed absence; worth a retry with different tooling in a future round. The original 28 January 2024 joint tripartite withdrawal declaration also was not located on any .gouv.ml or .ml government domain — it appears to have been announced via state broadcast media (ORTM) rather than published as a Journal Officiel or primature.ml document. UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF/G.21, processing Grok's round-2 follow-up): Grok supplied a full verbatim quote it claimed came from this same koulouba.ml page (a Jan 29 2024 Conseil extraordinaire, ministre Abdoulaye Diop citing 'trois principes' of sovereignty/partner-choice/vital-interest). Independently re-attempted this round with ~15 distinct methods — direct fetch, robots.txt probe, Wayback/archive.org, archive.ph, Google cache, Google Translate proxy, a reader proxy, and targeted web searches — koulouba.ml remained genuinely inaccessible throughout (fetcher could not even retrieve the domain's own robots.txt; a third-party reader proxy independently got its own 403 from the target, suggesting the site itself blocks non-browser fetchers). Search engines confirm a page with this exact title/URL is indexed, and a DIFFERENT primary Malian source (a July 2025 Diop interview, reported by saheltribune.com) independently corroborates the same 'trois principes' formulation as genuine recurring official language — but the specific verbatim paragraph Grok supplied remains UNVERIFIED against any primary text. Not minted; still a NOT FOUND for the exact quote, though the underlying event and phrasing pattern are plausible. Still worth a future browser-session (claude-in-chrome) retry given koulouba.ml appears to actively block non-browser fetchers specifically, not just fail generally.
